Upon defeat, releases a ring of 10 projectiles outward — the death burst must be dodged immediately after the kill shot lands
The spiral attack starts pointing downward, then makes a full rotation beginning toward Isaac's current direction — the predictable downward start allows pre-positioning
If Baby Plum takes no damage for 30 seconds, she waves and flies away, ending the fight without dying — the spare timer resets on any damage; only works in her dedicated boss room
A Chapter 1 airborne boss with a spare mechanic — her backward-propelling diagonal spit, two-ring ground slam, and post-death projectile ring each require different positioning
Spawns 2–3 holes in the floor from which its arms emerge to attack — arm attacks and head attacks alternate throughout the fight
Arms throw single or triple Troll Bombs at Isaac; the echo attack sends bombs into empty holes, causing hands to re-emerge from those holes throwing the same bomb type
Head attacks include a single large homing Dark Ball beneath itself, or a mix of 2 homing plus 1 non-homing Dark Ball fired simultaneously
Also fires a pair of large Dark Balls diagonally that bounce off walls rather than homing — wall bounces make their final positions less predictable than the homing variants
A brief window exists to kick a bomb into its open mouth during head attacks — this stuns Big Horn and causes it to take 20% increased damage while stunned
If Big Horn dies while performing a Dark Ball attack, Little Horn hops off its hand and continues the fight independently with low health
The ground slap arm attack strikes 3 times quickly while moving toward Isaac — it destroys any Dark Balls it contacts, inadvertently clearing the boss's own projectiles

A large underground boss from the Caves that alternates arm-from-hole and floating-head attacks — the bomb-into-mouth stun window and potential Little Horn continuation are its most distinctive mechanics
At approximately 50% HP, makes a final charge then permanently separates into two independent entities — a head and a body — each with distinct attack patterns
Phase 1: as Chimera builds speed, it leaves a persistent green creep trail — the faster it moves, the more of the arena it covers
The body in Phase 2 fires a Brimstone beam downward when Isaac is positioned directly above or below it — vertical positioning relative to the body determines laser exposure
In Phase 1, fires 8 Ipecac shots toward Isaac's predicted position with landing spots marked on the ground — the markers give brief pre-dodge warning
If one component dies first, the other adapts: the head switches to continuous wall-bouncing charges, the body switches to continuous rolling — killing both simultaneously is the safer approach
Gradually builds momentum in Phase 1; once fast enough, wide turns from momentum become a navigation hazard as significant as the attacks themselves
Phase 1 double jump: the first landing fires 8 tears outward in a ring; the second fires 4 diagonal rock waves — both triggers are a single jump sequence
A Repentance boss from the Corpse that builds speed leaving green creep, then splits into a head and body at half HP — both halves have conditional behavior based on which survives the other
Completely immune to damage while possessing a Clickety Clack — only vulnerable during the brief window when switching hosts or when all Clickety Clacks are eliminated and it is ejected
Spawns with 3 Clickety Clacks as possession vessels; non-possessed ones are shielded; a dead Clickety Clack leaves a purple fire that periodically fires bone projectiles
When all 3 Clickety Clacks are destroyed, Clutch is ejected and stunned — after sufficient damage it revives all 3 Clickety Clacks and the possession cycle restarts
At 25% HP, Clutch destroys all Clickety Clacks itself, leaving indestructible purple fires, and enters solo Phase 2 with bone orbitals blocking shots
In Phase 2, acquires bone orbitals that circle it and block tears — the orbital defense replaces the Phase 1 Clickety Clack immunity mechanic
Phase 2 attack: rushes to Isaac's position, stops, and fires six volleys of six purple flames each in an alternating directional pattern — repeats until death
The possessed Clickety Clack fires 8 bone shots in all cardinal and ordinal directions at moment of possession — the initial burst fires before resuming pursuit behavior

An Ashpit boss that possesses Clickety Clack vessels for immunity, revives them after full clearance, then goes solo with bone orbitals at 25% HP — the possession-swap mechanic is its most distinctive trait
Phase 1 slide attack leaves trails of explosive gas — the slide repeats until approximately 40% of the room floor is covered
Butt Bomb detonations ignite gas clouds, causing chain explosions across covered floor area — the bombs and accumulated gas form a combined mine system
At 50% HP, the containing bag explodes, creating explosive clouds and leaving Colostomia permanently adhered to the floor — Phase 2 attacks are entirely different from Phase 1
In Phase 2, jumps to a nearby location and fires 8 projectiles in a radial burst on landing, creating a brown creep puddle — only 2 creep puddles persist simultaneously
Phase 2 brown creep puddles accumulate from jump landings with a 2-puddle cap, limiting floor contamination from that attack type
Phase 2 also generates a ring of explosive gas around her position as a standalone fart attack — combined with any remaining Phase 1 gas, late-fight floor coverage can be extensive
Phase 2 twin-bomb spit launches 2 Butt Bombs at Isaac with throw range dependent on Isaac's proximity — closer positioning produces shorter-range, harder-to-dodge throws

An alt-Chapter 1 poop boss that mines the room with chained explosive gas in Phase 1, then adheres to the floor in Phase 2 — on death, her body diffuses into the arena water, turning it from green to brown
Spins to cause the room's water to circulate clockwise or counterclockwise — Isaac, Drips, Bombs, and Pickups are all caught in the current; negated by flight ability
Fires 4 spiraling projectile lines in two variants: slow with small gaps or fast with large gaps — gap size inversely relates to speed
The spiraling projectiles pass over poop for 1 second after firing, then are blocked by poop — the fight's poop obstacles can shield specific positions from the spirals
Periodically spits out Drip enemies, stopping once 4 are alive; the water circulation attack only activates when at least 2 Drips are present
Always stationary in the room center — all attacks fire outward from a fixed point, making diagonal positioning relative to Clog consistently the lowest-threat zone
The fart attack creates 3 spreading lines of knockback farts; each fart may spawn Poop, up to 3 total active Poops in the room
The fart lines spread across the room in 3 directions — the knockback can displace Isaac into Drip clusters or accumulated Poop obstacles
A stationary toilet-like boss from the alt-Chapter 1 floors — its room-water circulation current, poop-blocking spiral projectiles, and Flush!-style death are its most distinctive mechanics
Has no health bar — the fight consists of 6 enemy waves that must each be fully cleared; Great Gideon deactivates like a Stone Grimace after all waves are defeated
Periodically performs a vacuum that pulls Isaac, all enemies, and projectiles toward it — touching Great Gideon while the vacuum is active deals damage to Isaac
Fires 5 projectiles in a cone shape; the center projectile is larger and splits into 8 projectiles in a radial burst upon impact with anything

Starting from Wave 4, charges up and releases a rock wave down the arena center that breaks the floor creating gaps — always leaves at least 1 gap between created holes to prevent fully trapping Isaac
Spits large flame projectiles down the center of the arena; flames occasionally leave small fires behind and can transform enemies they hit into flaming variants
Never progresses a new enemy wave mid-attack — waves only begin after Great Gideon finishes its current attack cycle, creating reliable timing for wave transitions
Each of the 6 waves adds different enemy compositions; the enemies are the primary combat challenge while Great Gideon's own attacks create environmental pressure
A massive stone boss fought in a vertical double-size room — wave-based victory condition with no HP bar, vacuum pull, and a floor-breaking rock wave from Wave 4 onward define the encounter
Builds an orbital ring of up to 4 Willos in Phase 1; once at capacity, the Willos periodically fire 3 projectiles outward in a coordinated burst
Continuously spits out individual Willos to replenish the ring — the coordinated burst fires continuously even if individual Willos have been killed
In Phase 2, sheds her corpse husk and increases maximum orbital Willo capacity from 4 to 7 — ring density roughly doubles
Phase 2 introduces a chase attack where the entire orbiting Willo ring is sent to pursue Isaac for several seconds before returning
Phase 2 spawning attack: disappears and creates ground light clusters; Willos appear from each cluster, fire projectiles at Isaac, and vanish
Phase 2 can spawn up to 4 new Willos at once around herself, then causes all orbiting Willos to fire 3 projectiles outward simultaneously
Floats slowly and persistently toward Isaac throughout both phases — orbital reach compensates for her slow direct approach
A boss that builds an orbital Willo ring — Phase 2 doubles ring capacity to 7, adds a ring-chase attack, and introduces ground-spawn Willo ambushes
Four distinct phases: Phase 1 spawns Fistulas from damage thresholds, Phase 2 rapidly spawns short-lived Fistuloids, Phase 3 uses only direct attacks, Phase 4 transforms into a charging Chub
Continuously spawns Fistuloids up to 4 at once — only 1 chases Isaac at a time; others orbit and occasionally fire; a large blood projectile can kill the active chaser
In Phase 4, her Chub form is permanently orbited by Fistuloids that were orbiting before the transformation — the orbital ring carries over into the Chub fight
After taking 340 damage, Phase 2 triggers a rapid wave of short-lived Fistuloids with 20 HP — they lose health quickly on their own and shoot maggots almost immediately before dying
The Chubber jump attack launches 8 Chubber projectiles in all directions, which then rebound back toward The Matriarch — the returning shots create hazard in the space between Isaac and the boss
Phase 1 spawns 2 small Fistulas after 140 damage, then 2 more every 100 damage afterward — the Fistula count in the arena grows throughout Phase 1
A large blood projectile fires toward Isaac leaving red creep — can kill the actively chasing Fistuloid if it is in the path

A multi-phase cave boss that spawns Fistulas on taking damage, fires Fistuloid swarms in Phase 2, and transforms into a Chub in Phase 4 — the Chubber orbit-back mechanic distinguishes her from other summon bosses
Primary attack is a large fast cluster projectile that homes slightly on Isaac — on wall impact it explodes into projectiles, green creep, and maggots; below 50% HP fires 3 smaller clusters instead
Embeds a single tendril into a wall, then drags it along the wall surface, shooting projectiles, creep, and maggots out of the wall as it sweeps
The dual-tendril attack embeds 2 tendrils and rotates them while firing 2 simultaneous rings of 12 projectiles outward
The triangle trap fires 2 tendrils to either side of Isaac, trapping him in a triangle-shaped area — the attack cancels automatically if Isaac escapes before the follow-up projectile walls fire
Inside the triangle trap, fires walls of tight projectiles with navigable gaps plus faster direct shots at Isaac's current position
Floats quickly and attempts to stay above Isaac's position — the aerial positioning preference means the triangle trap is frequently deployed from above
Moves to the center and creates a spiral suction that pulls 2 tight projectile streams inward in a spiral pattern — direction switches randomly with additional projectiles filling gaps
A Corpse boss with tendril wall-embedding attacks — the dual-tendril ring rotation, triangle trap, and spiral suction define its encounter; instantly killed by Meat Cleaver
Charms up to 3 of Isaac's familiars, turning them against him — charmed familiars retain 60 HP and return to Isaac only when defeated
Sinks into the floor to chase Isaac while invulnerable, leaving a trail of slowing black creep — reappears with a swipe that fires 5 projectiles

Shockwave Scream emits 9 pulsating rings of projectiles expanding outward — each ring has an opening facing Isaac's current position, but the outward shockwave push complicates maintaining that alignment
The underground chase leaves a persistent slowing black creep trail — accumulated creep from multiple underground passes restricts movement throughout the fight

When fewer than 3 familiars are charmed, spawns Siren Minions and swipes them as a cluster toward Isaac — cluster wall collision kills the minions and releases a radial burst plus disorganized projectiles
Direct swipe attack fires 5 projectiles toward Isaac; the same spread fires on resurfacing from underground — two swipe-triggered spreads in quick succession are possible during the emerge sequence
Death burns away the body, leaving a skull behind — bombing the skull unlocks the Forgotten Lullaby trinket
An alt-Chapter 3 boss from the Mausoleum — familiar-charming and 9-ring shockwave are her most distinctive mechanics; defeating her leaves a bombable skull that unlocks the Forgotten Lullaby trinket
Constantly leaves a trail of slippery brown creep everywhere it moves — the entire fight area accumulates creep progressively throughout the encounter
After 7 seconds of normal movement, huddles its body and launches tail-first toward Isaac, straightening out mid-launch — transitions immediately into the spinning wall-bounce phase
After the tail-first launch, the head end spins around the tail while bouncing off walls at high speed before gradually decelerating to a stop
At 30 HP or less, splits into two 2-segment parts; each inherits the HP Turdlet had at split plus a 15 HP bonus — total HP increases rather than decreases at the transition
Moves with loose wall-bouncing chase behavior between launch attacks — the 7-second movement window between launches is the primary damage opportunity
After splitting, both halves continue leaving brown creep independently — two bodies moving between launch cycles can cover most of the arena
A 5-segment worm from the alt-Chapter 1 floors with a tail-first bouncing launch attack and a split Phase 2 that increases total HP rather than decreasing it
First attack in the fixed 5-attack cycle summons a Boom Fly orbited by 3 pink Eternal Fly Bombs
Second attack juggles 3 bombs and throws them toward Isaac — can have Hot Bombs or Sad Bombs effects
Third attack is an extended tear barrage escalating through many pattern stages — cardinal, diagonal, omnidirectional, rotating clusters, and spread volleys — ending with 3 cardinal fireballs
Fourth attack: teleports 3 times, throwing a short-delay Brimstone Bomb each time it repositions
Fifth attack: throws a Sad Bomb to create a smokescreen, then teleports 5 times while throwing Brimstone Bombs each time — the smokescreen delays visual tracking of the repositions
The Boom Fly from the first-cycle summon is orbited by 3 pink Eternal Fly Bombs — the orbital cluster moves with the Boom Fly as it roams the arena
Using Meat Cleaver splits The Horny Boys into a Hornfel and a Loki entity that each fight independently in their own attack patterns
An alt-Chapter 3 boss with a fixed, non-random 5-attack cycle — the extended tear barrage (attack 3) is the most complex sustained projectile sequence of any single boss attack in Repentance
